question: Can fixed, completed request histories alter identical probe verification budgets through shared online calibration, after common warmup and without concurrent requests?

histories.A: List the integers from 1 to 60 in ascending order, separated by commas.
histories.B: Write a short Python function that computes the greatest common divisor of two positive integers.

probe: List the integers from 1 to 30 in ascending order, separated by commas.
conditions: common checkpoint -> six A history requests learning enabled -> probe
common checkpoint -> six B history requests learning enabled -> probe
common checkpoint -> six A history requests and probe with estimator learning frozen
common checkpoint -> six B history requests and probe with estimator learning frozen
full restore to common checkpoint after B branch -> probe
controls: Every branch starts from the same idle common warm checkpoint; no resetting only theta
Warm refit kernel then restore its entire pre-warmup controller state; never force phase95 or inject synthetic observations in measured branches
No simultaneous requests; frontend and worker request maps must drain before branch/probe boundaries
Same target/draft/Full Attention architecture/BF16/K4/Triton/native sampler/graph shapes and decoding across all branches
Identical greedy probe ids are a correctness guard, not a quality or safety score
All history answers use ignore_eos with fixed caps; this controlled workload does not represent natural user traffic
No prompt search, seed sweep, model/backend change or adaptive extension after observing outcomes
record: All prompts, raw token ids and requested/actual generated lengths
Idle checkpoint digest, learning state, pending statistics and refit phase at each boundary
Every probe step: draft capacity, selected verification budget/admitted tokens, accepted/rejected counts, slot mapping and estimator phase
Native model/worker/attention/config identities and any kernel JIT events
Whole run failures and all zero-effect, improvement and degradation cases
pre_execution_requirements: Implement bounded worker-side observation hooks; verify transparent wrapping and meanings of budget/acceptance fields against pinned source

From the same restored common state compare one 32-token probe with hooks off and one with hooks on: at most two instrumentation engineering answers, token ids and controller learning state must match
Freeze exact prompts/order/code/hash and record engineering outcomes before starting the main screen
stop_or_interpretation: First runtime, restore, correctness or trace failure stops the run
If either learning history does not naturally cross at least one refit within six requests, report insufficient update exposure and stop without extending
Changed coefficients without changed probe verification allocation are not evidence of useful availability harm
Budget changes without robust measured user cost are only a mechanism observation
Timing is diagnostic only: synchronous tracing and remaining JIT effects preclude latency-harm claims
No natural-history attack, novelty or thesis viability conclusion from this pilot alone
